sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: That is the sound of exactly 2008 drummers pounding away in perfect synchronicity
sentences.zh: 刚才那阵声音，是整整2008名鼓手在完美同步地敲击，

sentences.en: during the opening ceremony of the 2008 Beijing Summer Olympics.
sentences.zh: 是在2008年北京夏季奥运会开幕式期间。

sentences.en: The entire stadium pitched into darkness as the traditional Chinese faux drums glowed from within.
sentences.zh: 整个体育场陷入黑暗，传统的中国缶从内部发出光芒。

sentences.en: It was just the start of a ceremony widely regarded as the most elaborate in Olympic
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是一场被广泛认为是奥运史上最精心制作的开幕式的开始，

sentences.en: history, and it was all designed and executed perfectly.
sentences.zh: 而且一切都设计和执行得非常完美。

sentences.en: But behind the scenes, there was one small hitch in the coverage of the event that went
sentences.zh: 但在幕后，这次活动的转播中出现了一个小插曲，

sentences.en: mostly unreported.
sentences.zh: 基本没有被报道过。

sentences.en: That's producer Daniel Simo.
sentences.zh: 那是制片人丹尼尔·西莫。

sentences.en: During the Parade of Nations, Greece, as the birthplace of the Olympics, entered firSt.
sentences.zh: 在运动员入场式中，作为奥运发源地的希腊第一个入场。

sentences.en: That's a longstanding tradition.
sentences.zh: 这是一个长久以来的传统。

sentences.en: But then the rest of the teams came out according to the number of strokes in the Chinese characters
sentences.zh: 但随后其余代表团是按照其名称的汉字笔画数入场的。

sentences.en: that comprise their name.
sentences.zh: （注：此处原文提及汉字笔画，实际奥运入场顺序为简体中文笔画数）

sentences.en: The country of Jamaica, for example, was followed by Belgium.
sentences.zh: 例如，牙买加之后是比利时。

sentences.en: Then came Vanuatu, which in turn was followed by Israel.
sentences.zh: 接着是瓦努阿图，随后是以色列。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: team walked out somewhere in the middle.
sentences.zh: 代表团走在中间的某个位置。

sentences.en: My home country of Australia was right at the back, 202nd in line.
sentences.zh: 我的祖国澳大利亚排在最后面，是第202个入场的。

sentences.en: Ultimately, the sequence of nations was just a small detail.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，国家入场的顺序只是一个小细节。

sentences.en: In a four-hour, $300 million ceremony, it should not have been the hard part.
sentences.zh: 在这一场四小时、耗资3亿美元的开幕式中，这本不该是难点。

sentences.en: But for the Western networks covering the games, the parade proved a little tricky.
sentences.zh: 但对于转播奥运会的西方电视网来说，这个入场式确实有点棘手。

sentences.en: Because it seems to us perfectly natural that the teams march in an alphabetical order.
sentences.zh: 因为在我们看来，代表团按字母顺序入场是再自然不过的事了。

sentences.en: That's Judith Flanders, author of A Place for Everything, a book about the order of the
sentences.zh: 那是朱迪思·弗兰德斯，《万物皆有位》的作者，这是一本关于

sentences.en: Latin alphabet.
sentences.zh: 拉丁字母顺序的书。

sentences.en: So it made all of the Western networks scramble because they simply didn't know when their
sentences.zh: 所以这让所有西方电视网手忙脚乱，因为他们根本不知道自己的

sentences.en: own teams were going to come in and when they could go to commercial breaks.
sentences.zh: 代表团何时入场，也不知道何时可以插播广告。

sentences.en: In the confusion of trying to figure out which countries came after which breaks, NBC later
sentences.zh: 在试图弄清楚哪些国家在哪些插播之后入场的混乱中，NBC后来

sentences.en: posted the footage to their website in the wrong order.
sentences.zh: 将视频上传到网站时弄错了顺序。

sentences.en: This in turn sparked a short-lived message board conspiracy theory that the networks had
sentences.zh: 这反过来引发了一个短暂的留言板阴谋论，称电视网

sentences.en: deliberately changed up the order of nations in order to increase site traffic.
sentences.zh: 故意打乱国家入场顺序，以增加网站流量。

sentences.en: You know, despite the fact that probably if you had asked the organizers doing the Olympic
sentences.zh: 你知道，尽管事实上如果你问那些负责奥运

sentences.en: coverage, they would have known that Chinese does not use an alphabet.
sentences.zh: 转播的组织者，他们本该知道中文是不使用字母表的。

sentences.en: But it didn't quite penetrate.
sentences.zh: 但这个事实并没有完全被理解。

sentences.en: So in that way, you see how deeply embedded the alphabet is in our psyches.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个角度看，你可以看出字母表在我们的潜意识中扎根有多深。

sentences.en: For much of the Western world, alphabetical order is the default.
sentences.zh: 对于大部分西方世界来说，字母顺序是默认设置。

sentences.en: It's often the one we try first, or the one we use as a last resort when all other ordering
sentences.zh: 它通常是我们首先尝试的方法，或者是在所有其他排序

sentences.en: methods fail.
sentences.zh: 方法都失败时使用的最后手段。

sentences.en: It's boring, but it works.
sentences.zh: 它很枯燥，但很有效。

sentences.en: And it's so ingrained that it's hard to imagine not using it.
sentences.zh: 而且它已经根深蒂固，以至于很难想象不使用它会怎样。

sentences.en: Except at one point, we didn't.
sentences.zh: 除非在某个时期，我们确实没有使用它。

sentences.en: Alphabetical order, as a way to organize information, is a pretty recent development.
sentences.zh: 作为一种组织信息的方式，字母顺序是一个相当近期的发展。

sentences.en: And its adoption is part of a radical shift in the way human beings learn, organize their
sentences.zh: 它的采用是人类学习、组织

sentences.en: thoughts, and even see their place in the world.
sentences.zh: 思想，甚至看待自身在世界中位置的方式发生根本性转变的一部分。

sentences.en: But before you can order anything alphabetically, you need an alphabet.
sentences.zh: 但在你能按字母顺序排列任何东西之前，你需要一个字母表。

sentences.en: The alphabet is a concept of applying symbols to sounds and saying this stands for this and
sentences.zh: 字母表是一个将符号应用于声音的概念，即这个符号代表这个声音，而且

sentences.en: this only.
sentences.zh: 仅代表这个声音。

sentences.en: That's Timothy Donaldson, a type designer and lecturer at Falmouth University in England and
sentences.zh: 那是蒂莫西·唐纳森，一位字体设计师，英国法尔茅斯大学讲师，

sentences.en: author of the book Shapes for Sounds.
sentences.zh: 也是《声音的形状》一书的作者。

sentences.en: And Donaldson says that the process of assigning sounds to symbols took a long time.
sentences.zh: 唐纳森说，将声音分配给符号的过程花费了很长时间。

sentences.en: Because at first, all we had were pictograms, images that represented whole objects or concepts,
sentences.zh: 因为起初，我们只有象形文字，即代表整个物体或概念的图像，

sentences.en: like in very early Sumerian writing.
sentences.zh: 就像在非常早期的苏美尔文字中那样。

sentences.en: So if you wanted to represent the idea of a fish, you drew a fish.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想表达“鱼”的概念，你就画一条鱼。

sentences.en: But what the problem it brings with it is you need a massive amount of symbols.
sentences.zh: 但随之而来的问题是，你需要大量的符号。

sentences.en: You need thousands of symbols to represent every single thing.
sentences.zh: 你需要成千上万的符号来代表每一个事物。

sentences.en: So the system is unwieldy.
sentences.zh: 所以这个系统很笨重。

sentences.en: Eventually, these pictograms changed and became more abstract.
sentences.zh: 最终，这些象形文字发生了变化，变得更加抽象。

sentences.en: And by 2800 BCE, certain marks began to represent syllables.
sentences.zh: 到了公元前2800年，某些标记开始代表音节。

sentences.en: But not individual consonants or vowels.
sentences.zh: 但不是单独的辅音或元音。

sentences.en: So there might be a symbol for an entire syllable, like ga, but nothing yet for its component
sentences.zh: 所以可能有一个符号代表整个音节，比如“ga”，但还没有符号代表其组成部分

sentences.en: ga and a sounds individually, meaning each syllable in a language needed a sign.
sentences.zh: “g”和“a”的单独声音，这意味着语言中的每个音节都需要一个符号。

sentences.en: And they could get by with about 700 symbols.
sentences.zh: 他们大约需要700个符号才能应付。

sentences.en: We call that a syllabary.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为音节文字。

sentences.en: But a syllabary still isn't an alphabet.
sentences.zh: 但音节文字仍然不是字母表。

sentences.en: But at some point, some clever, early Semitic-speaking someone saw that the Egyptians were writing stuff
sentences.zh: 但在某个时候，某个聪明的早期闪米特语使用者看到埃及人在写东西，

sentences.en: down and said, hey, we can do that for my language.
sentences.zh: 于是说，嘿，我们可以用这种方法来写我的语言。

sentences.en: And that's Peter Daniels, an independent scholar specializing in ancient writing systeMs.
sentences.zh: 那是彼得·丹尼尔斯，一位专门研究古代书写系统的独立学者。

sentences.en: Daniels says that the Egyptians were using their own complicated, non-syllabic system of symbols.
sentences.zh: 丹尼尔斯说，埃及人当时使用的是他们自己复杂的、非音节的符号系统。

sentences.en: When a hypothetical early Semitic someone decided to take that Egyptian system and simplify it.
sentences.zh: 当某个假设的早期闪米特人决定采用并简化那个埃及系统时，

sentences.en: Because this clever inventor had the brilliant idea to use just one consonant per letter.
sentences.zh: 因为这位聪明的发明家有一个绝妙的主意，即每个字母只使用一个辅音。

sentences.en: Still no vowels, but with those consonants, they could write anything that needed to be written.
sentences.zh: 虽然还没有元音，但有了这些辅音，他们就能写下任何需要写的东西。

sentences.en: Developing what some scholars considered to be the first true alphabet.
sentences.zh: 这发展成了某些学者认为的第一个真正的字母表。

sentences.en: And with it, the first alphabetical order.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的，是第一种字母顺序。

sentences.en: And that first ever alphabetical order would be instantly recognizable.
sentences.zh: 而那第一个字母顺序会让人一眼就能认出来。

sentences.en: It's the same basic order that the Latin alphabet uses today.
sentences.zh: 它与今天拉丁字母使用的基本顺序相同。

sentences.en: In the 1940s, archaeologists found a set of small tablets with some 3,200-year-old lettering
sentences.zh: 20世纪40年代，考古学家在现今叙利亚的古城乌加里特发现了一组小泥板，

sentences.en: in the ancient city of Ugarit in present-day Syria.
sentences.zh: 上面刻有约3200年前的文字。

sentences.en: With nothing on them but the 30 letters of the Ugaritic alphabet.
sentences.zh: 上面除了乌加里特字母表的30个字母外别无他物。

sentences.en: And they were all written in the familiar order that became A, B, C, D, E, F, etc.
sentences.zh: 而且它们都是按照后来演变成A、B、C、D、E、F等熟悉的顺序书写的。

sentences.en: Everything from A to T.
sentences.zh: 从A到T的所有字母。

sentences.en: T was the last letter in that particular alphabetical order.
sentences.zh: T是那个特定字母顺序中的最后一个字母。

sentences.en: The exact shapes of the Ugaritic letters would go through a lot of changes as they got adapted.
sentences.zh: 乌加里特字母的具体形状在被改编的过程中经历了许多变化。

sentences.en: Early on by the Phoenicians, then the Greeks, and later the Romans.
sentences.zh: 早期由腓尼基人，然后是希腊人，后来是罗马人。

sentences.en: But the basic order was there from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 但基本顺序从一开始就存在了。

sentences.en: But that raises a fundamental question.
sentences.zh: 但这提出了一个根本性的问题。

sentences.en: Why that order?
sentences.zh: 为什么是那个顺序？

sentences.en: Why A, B, C, and not N, Q, D, or R, G, L?
sentences.zh: 为什么是A、B、C，而不是N、Q、D，或者R、G、L？

sentences.en: And the answer is...
sentences.zh: 答案是……

sentences.en: Well, we don't know.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们不知道。

sentences.en: It was a long time ago.
sentences.zh: 那是很久以前的事了。

sentences.en: Okay, fair.
sentences.zh: 好吧，有道理。

sentences.en: There's no particular reason.
sentences.zh: 没有特别的原因。

sentences.en: We just learn the alphabet in the order it's in.
sentences.zh: 我们只是按照字母表现在的顺序来学习它。

sentences.en: There was, however, at least one competing alphabetical order from around that same time,
sentences.zh: 然而，在大约同一时期，至少存在一种相互竞争的字母顺序，

sentences.en: found in the southern Arabian peninsula in present-day Yemen and Oman.
sentences.zh: 在现今也门和阿曼所在的阿拉伯半岛南部被发现。

sentences.en: So, similar alphabet, but different sequence.
sentences.zh: 所以，字母表相似，但顺序不同。

sentences.en: It went H, L, a strange-looking letter I can't pronounce or recognize, M, R, etc.
sentences.zh: 它是H、L，一个我无法发音或识别的奇怪字母，M、R，等等。

sentences.en: But outside of a few small areas, this other order never caught on.
sentences.zh: 但在少数几个小区域之外，这种顺序从未流行起来。

sentences.en: And for the usual reason.
sentences.zh: 原因也很常见。

sentences.en: The one that won out was the one that was used by the people that went out and conquered other people.
sentences.zh: 胜出的那个顺序，是被那些出去征服其他民族的人所使用的顺序。

sentences.en: That just happens.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样发生的。

sentences.en: The South Arabian people were more limited in their conquering.
sentences.zh: 南阿拉伯人的征服范围比较有限。

sentences.en: The Romans, on the other hand, loved conquering.
sentences.zh: 而罗马人则热爱征服。

sentences.en: And as they conquered, they spread their alphabetical order around.
sentences.zh: 随着他们的征服，他们传播了自己的字母顺序。

sentences.en: Although not before making some last-minute tweaks.
sentences.zh: 当然，在传播之前他们做了一些临时的调整。

sentences.en: Take the final two letters, Y and Z.
sentences.zh: 看看最后两个字母，Y和Z。

sentences.en: The Romans didn't use them.
sentences.zh: 罗马人并不使用它们。

sentences.en: Tim Donaldson says that the ancient Greek equivalents of Y and Z had previously been dispersed in the middle of the Greek alphabet.
sentences.zh: 蒂姆·唐纳森说，古希腊语中Y和Z的对应字母之前分散在希腊字母表的中间。

sentences.en: But then the Romans chucked them out.
sentences.zh: 但后来罗马人把它们踢出去了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, that was literally how it happened.
sentences.zh: 是的，事情就是这样发生的。

sentences.en: And then eventually they found that they were useful, so they got brought back into the fold.
sentences.zh: 后来他们发现这些字母很有用，于是又把它们收了回来。

sentences.en: But that's why they're at the end.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么它们排在最后。

sentences.en: The letter K was luckier.
sentences.zh: 字母K比较幸运。

sentences.en: It was also kicked out at some point, but then brought back in at the same spot as before.
sentences.zh: 它也曾一度被踢出，但后来又被放回了原来的位置。

sentences.en: They also tried to introduce three new Roman letters.
sentences.zh: 他们还试图引入三个新的罗马字母。

sentences.en: And it just didn't work.
sentences.zh: 但没成功。

sentences.en: What were the letters?
sentences.zh: 是什么字母？

sentences.en: One was called Di Gamma.
sentences.zh: 一个叫Di Gamma。

sentences.en: And one looks, I can't remember the name of the other two, even though I wrote a book about it.
sentences.zh: 还有一个看起来……我不记得另外两个的名字了，尽管我写过一本关于它的书。

sentences.en: So, for the most part, the alphabet's order has proved remarkably stable.
sentences.zh: 所以，在很大程度上，字母表的顺序被证明是非常稳定的。

sentences.en: But despite its endurance, for most of its history, alphabetical order wasn't actually used to order much of anything.
sentences.zh: 但尽管它很持久，在其大部分历史中，字母顺序实际上并没有被用来排列很多东西。

sentences.en: Alphabetical order was not all that important for anything beyond learning the alphabet.
sentences.zh: 除了学习字母表本身，字母顺序在其他方面并不是那么重要。

sentences.en: In societies like ancient Rome and early medieval Europe, writing implements were still rare.
sentences.zh: 在古罗马和中世纪早期的欧洲等社会，书写工具仍然很稀缺。

sentences.en: So what mattered most was organizing knowledge in a way that helped you to memorize it.
sentences.zh: 所以最重要的是以一种有助于记忆的方式组织知识。

sentences.en: And that was usually much easier to do in the order you naturally came across the information.
sentences.zh: 而这通常以你自然接触到信息的顺序来做要容易得多。

sentences.en: So you might memorize the names of kings in chronological order, following who begat who.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会按时间顺序记住国王的名字，追溯谁生了谁。

sentences.en: Or all the towns along the coastline, from east to weSt.
sentences.zh: 或者按从东到西的顺序记住沿海的所有城镇。

sentences.en: And Judith Flander says that this means, in most cases, alphabetical order would have been kind of useless.
sentences.zh: 朱迪思·弗兰德斯说，这意味着在大多数情况下，字母顺序几乎是没用的。

sentences.en: And the way I've begun to think of it is to say to people,
sentences.zh: 我开始思考这个问题的方式是告诉人们：

sentences.en: OK, put the days of the week in alphabetical order.
sentences.zh: 好，把一周的七天按字母顺序排列。

sentences.en: Let's see.
sentences.zh: 让我看看。

sentences.en: Friday.
sentences.zh: 星期五。

sentences.en: Monday.
sentences.zh: 星期一。

sentences.en: And there's always a very long pause.
sentences.zh: 总是会有很长的停顿。

sentences.en: Thursday, Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 星期四，星期二。

sentences.en: Because we don't think of them that way.
sentences.zh: 因为我们不是那样思考它们的。

sentences.en: We start at Monday.
sentences.zh: 我们从星期一开始。

sentences.en: Saturday, Sunday, Wednesday.
sentences.zh: 星期六，星期日，星期三。

sentences.en: Jesus.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: So when it came to sorting and organizing actual information, for thousands of years, people used almost any other method.
sentences.zh: 所以当涉及到分类和组织实际信息时，几千年来，人们几乎使用了任何其他方法。

sentences.en: They organized things by size, by geography, by chronology.
sentences.zh: 他们按大小、地理、时间顺序来组织事物。

sentences.en: Just not alphabetically.
sentences.zh: 就是不按字母顺序。

sentences.en: But these early ordering methods also reflected the way people thought about the world.
sentences.zh: 但这些早期的排序方法也反映了人们看待世界的方式。

sentences.en: And one important way that they thought about it was hierarchically.
sentences.zh: 他们看待世界的一个重要方式是等级制度。

sentences.en: In the Middle Ages, for example, William the Conqueror's doomsday book, which was a survey of all his subjects' property assets,
sentences.zh: 例如，在中世纪，威廉征服者的《末日审判书》，这是一份对他所有臣民财产资产的调查，

sentences.en: was divided into sections that started with the nobles and ended with the peasants.
sentences.zh: 被分为若干部分，从贵族开始，到农民结束。

sentences.en: So you move down not alphabetically, but through more or less who had more money and who had more power.
sentences.zh: 所以你向下移动时不是按字母顺序，而是或多或少按谁更有钱、谁更有权来排列。

sentences.en: Church documents also tended to reflect this hierarchical view.
sentences.zh: 教会文件也倾向于反映这种等级观念。

sentences.en: Where the church fathers come first, and then other theological writers, then other less important writers,
sentences.zh: 教会教父排在前面，然后是其他神学作家，再然后是其他不那么重要的作家。

sentences.en: and finally whisper, pagan writers, they weren't even Christian.
sentences.zh: 最后还要悄悄说一句，那些异教徒作家，他们甚至都不是基督徒。

sentences.en: And they trail in at the end because they're not important.
sentences.zh: 他们被排在最后，因为他们并不重要。

sentences.en: But nowhere was this hierarchical worldview more apparent than in encyclopedias.
sentences.zh: 但这种等级森严的世界观，在百科全书中体现得最为明显。

sentences.en: These books were primarily religious documents, written by archbishops and monks,
sentences.zh: 这些书主要是宗教文献，由大主教和僧侣撰写，

sentences.en: who were attempting to create what they called a mirror of the world.
sentences.zh: 他们试图创造出他们所谓的“世界之镜”。

sentences.en: Starting with God, the angels, and the saints at the front, and plants and inanimate objects at the very back.
sentences.zh: 开头是上帝、天使和圣徒，结尾则是植物和无生命物体。

sentences.en: Humans were usually somewhere in the middle.
sentences.zh: 人类通常被放在中间位置。

sentences.en: Theological books might have glossaries of difficult terms at the back.
sentences.zh: 神学书籍的末尾可能会有难词词汇表。

sentences.en: But these would be organized in the order they appear in the book, not alphabetically.
sentences.zh: 但这些词汇是按它们在书中出现的顺序排列的，而不是按字母顺序。

sentences.en: Because in a world where knowledge was considered complete and holistic,
sentences.zh: 因为在一个被认为知识是完整且整体的世界里，

sentences.en: the point was not to look up only the facts you needed, but to read the book from beginning to end.
sentences.zh: 重点不在于只查找你需要的事实，而在于从头到尾阅读整本书。

sentences.en: You might occasionally come across a merchant's invoice or one small part of a dictionary organized alphabetically.
sentences.zh: 你偶尔可能会遇到商人的发票或字典中按字母顺序排列的一小部分。

sentences.en: But even as late as the Middle Ages, alphabetical order was still so rare
sentences.zh: 但即使到了中世纪晚期，字母顺序依然非常罕见，

sentences.en: that anytime someone used it in a book, they would have to explain it.
sentences.zh: 以至于每当有人在书中使用它时，都必须加以解释。

sentences.en: So you'd get this kind of primer from the author at the beginning, where he might say,
sentences.zh: 所以你会看到作者在书的开头写一段入门说明，他可能会说，

sentences.en: if the topic you're interested in starts with Z, try looking towards the end.
sentences.zh: 如果你感兴趣的主题以Z开头，试着往后翻。

sentences.en: And it's perfectly clear he thinks he has invented it.
sentences.zh: 而且很明显，他认为这是他发明的。

sentences.en: And then each time another person uses it, they too explain it over and over.
sentences.zh: 然后每当另一个人使用它时，他们也会一遍又一遍地解释。

sentences.en: Slowly though, little by little, alphabetical order would start to catch on.
sentences.zh: 不过，字母顺序还是慢慢地、一点一点地流行起来了。

sentences.en: We can't say why exactly, but Judith Flanders points to one potential reason,
sentences.zh: 我们无法确切说明原因，但朱迪丝·弗兰德斯指出了一个潜在原因，

sentences.en: at least for those who knew their ABCs.
sentences.zh: 至少对于那些认识字母表的人来说是这样。

sentences.en: Every other sorting order, you need to know a little bit about the subject to help you find things.
sentences.zh: 对于其他任何排序方式，你都需要对主题有所了解才能找到东西。

sentences.en: Alphabetical order is the only sorting order that we have where you do not need to have any preliminary knowledge.
sentences.zh: 字母顺序是我们拥有的唯一一种不需要任何预备知识的排序方式。

sentences.en: And this proved useful in a world where increasingly there was just too much to remember.
sentences.zh: 在一个需要记忆的东西越来越多的世界里，这被证明非常有用。

sentences.en: In the 11th and 12th centuries, with the arrival of paper technology from China,
sentences.zh: 在11和12世纪，随着中国造纸技术的传入，

sentences.en: writing something down started to become a lot cheaper and more attractive than trying to memorize it.
sentences.zh: 把事情写下来开始变得比试图背诵它便宜得多，也更有吸引力。

sentences.en: For theology students at European universities, this helped facilitate a new form of learning.
sentences.zh: 对于欧洲大学的神学学生来说，这有助于促进一种新的学习形式。

sentences.en: One in which arguments and counter-arguments were expected to be backed up by written evidence.
sentences.zh: 在这种形式中，论点和反驳都需要有书面证据支持。

sentences.en: But it also meant that now, you had to know where to find all those sources, so you could cite them correctly.
sentences.zh: 但这同时也意味着，你现在必须知道去哪里找到所有这些来源，以便正确引用它们。

sentences.en: So scholars began developing innovative ways to search for information, indexing, pagination,
sentences.zh: 于是学者们开始开发创新的信息搜索方式，如索引、页码，

sentences.en: methods for cross-referencing one thing with another.
sentences.zh: 以及交叉引用不同事物的方法。

sentences.en: And this brings with it the development of all of these things that help us locate things,
sentences.zh: 这带来了所有这些帮助我们定位事物的工具的发展，

sentences.en: or as I call it, look stuff up.
sentences.zh: 或者正如我所说的，就是“查东西”。

sentences.en: We become a look stuff up world.
sentences.zh: 我们变成了一个“查东西”的世界。

sentences.en: And one of the handiest ways to look stuff up was simply by name.
sentences.zh: 而“查东西”最方便的方法之一就是直接按名字查找。

sentences.en: With alphabetical order, you didn't need to be an expert in a field to know where to find something.
sentences.zh: 有了字母顺序，你不需要成为某个领域的专家也能知道去哪里找到东西。

sentences.en: All you needed to know was how to spell it.
sentences.zh: 你唯一需要知道的就是怎么拼写它。

sentences.en: Travelling Franciscan preachers, for example, might not actually have that much religious education.
sentences.zh: 例如，四处奔走的方济各会传教士，他们可能并没有受过太多的宗教教育。

sentences.en: But now, they would have a small booklet with them,
sentences.zh: 但现在，他们随身带着一本小册子，

sentences.en: which would provide talking points on different subjects from the Bible,
sentences.zh: 里面提供了圣经中不同主题的谈话要点，

sentences.en: just in time for their next sermon.
sentences.zh: 正好赶上他们的下一次布道。

sentences.en: So what these were is, effectively, they were cheat sheets.
sentences.zh: 所以这些东西实际上就是小抄。

sentences.en: And to make them easier to use, they were put in alphabetical order.
sentences.zh: 为了使用方便，它们被按字母顺序排列。

sentences.en: Another big factor in the rise of alphabetical order was the arrival in the 15th century of the printing press.
sentences.zh: 字母顺序兴起的另一个重要因素是15世纪印刷机的出现。

sentences.en: Now that books were easy to copy, publishers realized they could make big money selling multiple copies of a single title.
sentences.zh: 现在书籍容易复制了，出版商意识到他们可以通过销售同一书名的多个副本赚大钱。

sentences.en: And the bestsellers often turned out to be reference books.
sentences.zh: 而畅销书往往是参考书。

sentences.en: At first, many of these reference books still strived to be mirrors of the world, organized hierarchically.
sentences.zh: 起初，许多参考书仍然努力成为“世界之镜”，按等级排列。

sentences.en: But as Enlightenment encyclopedists like Diderot incorporated more and more entries from more and more contributors,
sentences.zh: 但随着像狄德罗这样的启蒙运动百科全书编纂者纳入了越来越多贡献者的条目，

sentences.en: the easiest way to add a new entry without shuffling everything else around was just to organize it alphabetically.
sentences.zh: 在不打乱其他内容的情况下添加新条目的最简单方法，就是按字母顺序排列。

sentences.en: And so, they cite the great hierarchy schemes, but they don't use it.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们引用了伟大的等级体系方案，但并没有使用它。

sentences.en: And instead, they say, they're going to use alphabetical order because it is plus commode et plus facile, more convenient and easier.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们说，他们要使用字母顺序，因为它“更方便、更容易”。

sentences.en: But even as scholars were busy alphabetizing the angels,
sentences.zh: 但即使学者们忙于给天使按字母排序时，

sentences.en: other members of the establishment weren't happy about this new method of dividing up the world.
sentences.zh: 体制内的其他人对这种划分世界的新方法并不满意。

sentences.en: To understand why, Flanders points to a 16th century bibliography dedicated to the King of France.
sentences.zh: 为了理解原因，弗兰德斯提到了16世纪献给法国国王的一部书目。

sentences.en: And the compiler apologizes in his preface for putting it in alphabetical order.
sentences.zh: 编纂者在序言中为将其按字母顺序排列而道歉。

sentences.en: Because, he says, this might mean servants come before masters and children before their parents.
sentences.zh: 因为他说，这可能意味着仆人排在主人前面，孩子排在父母前面。

sentences.en: It upends hierarchy and it is dangerous.
sentences.zh: 这颠覆了等级制度，是危险的。

sentences.en: Even worse, this was a way of organizing knowledge that allowed any literate person to choose what to learn.
sentences.zh: 更糟糕的是，这是一种允许任何识字的人选择学习内容的知识组织方式。

sentences.en: With alphabetical order, knowledge was no longer a fixed set of ideas to be handed down by learned authorities.
sentences.zh: 有了字母顺序，知识不再是由权威学者传授的固定观念集。

sentences.en: Instead, it was up to the individual to decide what was worth discovering and what could be ignored.
sentences.zh: 相反，由个人决定什么值得发现，什么可以忽略。

sentences.en: So, if you've got gatekeepers to knowledge, those gatekeepers are going to think, we're going to be out of work soon.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你有知识的守门人，这些守门人就会想，我们很快就要失业了。

sentences.en: And this feeling wasn't just restricted to a bunch of royal reactionaries in the 1500s.
sentences.zh: 这种感觉不仅仅局限于1500年代的一群保皇派反动分子。

sentences.en: Alphabetical order's biggest hater was probably the early 19th century English poet, Samuel Taylor Coleridge.
sentences.zh: 字母顺序最大的仇敌可能是19世纪初的英国诗人塞缪尔·泰勒·柯勒律治。

sentences.en: Coleridge.
sentences.zh: 柯勒律治。

sentences.en: He just despised it.
sentences.zh: 他简直厌恶它。

sentences.en: Coleridge saved a special place in hell for the Encyclopedia Britannica, which was, of course, organized alphabetically.
sentences.zh: 柯勒律治为《大英百科全书》在地狱里留了一个特殊的位置，因为它当然是按字母顺序排列的。

sentences.en: As a theologian, as well as a poet, he believed in the great hierarchy of knowledge.
sentences.zh: 作为一名神学家兼诗人，他相信伟大的知识等级体系。

sentences.en: And he thought Britain's preeminent reference book should reflect that.
sentences.zh: 他认为英国最杰出的参考书应该反映这一点。

sentences.en: And he said, yes, it reflects the world.
sentences.zh: 他说，是的，它反映了世界。

sentences.en: But once it's in this arbitrary and he thought ridiculous order, Apple comes first just because it starts with A, what you've got is a broken mirror on the ground,
sentences.zh: 但一旦它处于这种武断的、他认为荒谬的顺序中——苹果排在第一位仅仅因为它以A开头——你得到的就是一面碎在地上的镜子，

sentences.en: each reflecting a little bit of the world, but making no overall sense.
sentences.zh: 每一片都反映了一点点世界，但整体上毫无意义。

sentences.en: Which, I'll admit, as far as literary criticism goes, is kind of beautiful.
sentences.zh: 我得承认，就文学批评而言，这还挺美的。

sentences.en: I mean, he was a poet.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他毕竟是个诗人。

sentences.en: But he was also a snob, the kind of substack writing intellectual that alphabetical order had been undermining all along.
sentences.zh: 但他也是个势利小人，那种字母顺序一直以来都在削弱的Substack写作知识分子。

sentences.en: So, if anything, his objections made him seem a little out of touch.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果说有什么的话，他的反对意见让他显得有点脱离现实。

sentences.en: He was even parodied in novels as, quote,
sentences.zh: 他甚至在小说中被戏仿为，引用：

sentences.en: The chemical, botanical, geological, astronomical, mathematical, metaphysical, meteorological, anatomical, physiological, galvanistical, musical, pictorial, bibliographical,
sentences.zh: 化学、植物学、地质学、天文学、数学、形而上学、气象学、解剖学、生理学、电学、音乐、绘画、书目学，

sentences.en: crucial, philosopher.
sentences.zh: 关键的哲学家。

sentences.en: In other words, he was an insufferable know-it-all.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他是个令人难以忍受的万事通。

sentences.en: The truth is, by the time guys like Coleridge were shouting at alphabetical order to get off their lawn, the battle was already over.
sentences.zh: 事实是，当像柯勒律治这样的人对着字母顺序大喊大叫让他们滚开时，战斗早已结束了。

sentences.en: At some point, when no one was looking, without needing a great champion to advance it or a campaign to promote it, alphabetical order had won.
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，当没人注意时，不需要伟大的拥护者去推动，也不需要运动去宣传，字母顺序就已经赢了。

sentences.en: And other possibilities sort of faded.
sentences.zh: 而其他的可能性就那样消失了。

sentences.en: People lost sight of the fact that there are other possibilities.
sentences.zh: 人们忽略了还有其他可能性这一事实。

sentences.en: Today, organizing information according to its name has become so commonplace that it often just goes unnoticed.
sentences.zh: 今天，根据名称组织信息已经变得如此普遍，以至于经常被忽视。

sentences.en: But it still comes with its own biases.
sentences.zh: 但它仍然带有自身的偏见。

sentences.en: Just ask anyone whose name starts with a letter at the end of the alphabet.
sentences.zh: 问问任何名字以字母表末尾字母开头的人就知道了。

sentences.en: Academic economists are more likely to be cited, get jobs at prestigious universities,
sentences.zh: 学术经济学家如果名字在字母表中靠前，更有可能被引用、在名牌大学获得工作，

sentences.en: and even win Nobel Prizes if their names are higher up in the alphabet.
sentences.zh: 甚至获得诺贝尔奖。

sentences.en: Political candidates are more likely to win if they have early alphabet names rather than late names.
sentences.zh: 政治候选人如果名字在字母表中靠前，比名字靠后的人更有可能获胜。

sentences.en: There is even something called alphabet fatigue,
sentences.zh: 甚至还有一种东西叫“字母疲劳”，

sentences.en: which is a phenomenon where a dictionary or encyclopedia team becomes less and less thorough as they move through the letters.
sentences.zh: 这是一种现象，即字典或百科全书团队在处理字母时会变得越来越不彻底。

sentences.en: The first alphabetized edition of Encyclopedia Britannica had three volumes, each of roughly equal length.
sentences.zh: 第一版按字母顺序排列的《大英百科全书》有三卷，每卷长度大致相等。

sentences.en: Volume one was A through B.
sentences.zh: 第一卷是A到B。

sentences.en: And of course, as we know, there are plenty of cultures and languages and civilizations that have done perfectly nicely without an alphabet.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们知道，有很多文化、语言和文明在没有字母表的情况下也过得很好。

sentences.en: And they have no problem with other sorting systeMs.
sentences.zh: 他们对其他排序系统没有任何问题。

sentences.en: During the Ming Dynasty in 15th century China, the largest general encyclopedia in history was organized according to a well-known rhyming scheme.
sentences.zh: 在15世纪中国明朝时期，历史上最大的综合性百科全书是根据一种著名的韵律方案组织的。

sentences.en: It remained the world's largest reference book for six centuries.
sentences.zh: 它保持了六个世纪的世界最大参考书地位。

sentences.en: And it worked just fine.
sentences.zh: 而且它运行得很好。

sentences.en: And in the 21st century, people have started turning to other ways of finding and sorting information.
sentences.zh: 到了21世纪，人们开始转向其他寻找和排序信息的方式。

sentences.en: Even as much of the internet's underlying infrastructure depends on it,
sentences.zh: 尽管互联网的大部分底层基础设施都依赖于它，

sentences.en: no one uses alphabetical order to search through Wikipedia or to decide which article to click on next.
sentences.zh: 但没有人会用字母顺序来搜索维基百科或决定接下来点击哪篇文章。

sentences.en: Instead of indexes organized alphabetically, we have hyperlinks leading in a thousand different directions.
sentences.zh: 我们不再使用按字母顺序排列的索引，而是拥有指向一千个不同方向的超链接。

sentences.en: Alphabetical order may have won when no one was looking.
sentences.zh: 字母顺序可能是在没人注意的时候赢得了胜利。

sentences.en: But now, just as quietly, it's being rendered obsolete.
sentences.zh: 但现在，它正悄无声息地变得过时。

sentences.en: So we may discover that alphabetical order is a phase.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可能会发现，字母顺序只是一个阶段。

sentences.en: An 8th century phase, but it might be a phase.
sentences.zh: 一个8世纪的阶段，但它可能只是一个阶段。

sentences.en: Do you have a coda for this story?
sentences.zh: 你对这个故事有什么尾声吗？

sentences.en: Yes, we do.
sentences.zh: 是的，有的。

sentences.en: After this.
sentences.zh: 在这之后。

sentences.en: So we're here again with Daniel Simo.
sentences.zh: 我们又和丹尼尔·西莫在一起了。

sentences.en: Hey, Dan.
sentences.zh: 嘿，丹。

sentences.en: Hey, Roman.
sentences.zh: 嘿，罗曼。

sentences.en: Before I let you go, I heard you have one more thing that you wanted to share with us regarding alphabetical order.
sentences.zh: 在你走之前，我听说你还有一件事想和我们分享，关于字母顺序的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I do.
sentences.zh: 是的，我有。

sentences.en: And I wanted to save it for the coda because, you know, as a reporter, one of the things I love the most is when someone I'm interviewing really hates one of their subjects.
sentences.zh: 我想把它留到尾声再说，因为你知道，作为一名记者，我最喜欢的事情之一就是当我采访的人真的很讨厌他们的某个研究对象时。

sentences.en: And it turns out that Judith Flanders really, really hates someone.
sentences.zh: 结果朱迪丝·弗兰德斯真的、真的很讨厌某个人。

sentences.en: And I found this out towards the end of the interview when I was wrapping things up.
sentences.zh: 我在采访快结束、准备收尾时发现了这一点。

sentences.en: And I asked my standard kind of wrap-up question, and I just want to play you some of that tape.
sentences.zh: 我问了标准的收尾问题，我想给你们放一段录音。

sentences.en: Judith, is there anything that we haven't touched on that you think would be important to mention?
sentences.zh: 朱迪丝，还有什么我们没谈到但你认为值得一提的重要事情吗？

sentences.en: There isn't.
sentences.zh: 没有了。

sentences.en: The only thing I wonder if you want me to do, just because you said you wanted a couple of sort of character-driven things, is the hideous Melville Dewey.
sentences.zh: 我唯一想问你是否想让我做的是，因为你说过想要一些以人物为驱动的内容，那就是那个可恶的梅尔维尔·杜威。

sentences.en: At which point you're like, oh, yes, please, talk about the hideous Melville Dewey.
sentences.zh: 这时候你就会说，哦，是的，请谈谈那个可恶的梅尔维尔·杜威。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yes, please.
sentences.zh: 是的，请讲。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, Dewey is not interesting in terms of alphabetical order, except he didn't use it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你知道，杜威在字母顺序方面没什么意思，除非他根本没用它。

sentences.en: But he was so ghastly.
sentences.zh: 但他太糟糕了。

sentences.en: I mean, apart from anything else, the moron spelt his name, M-E-L-V-I-L.
sentences.zh: 我是说，撇开其他不谈，那个白痴把自己的名字拼成 M-E-L-V-I-L。

sentences.en: I mean, really?
sentences.zh: 我是说，真的吗？

sentences.en: I didn't think I could love Judith Flanders anymore, but I really enjoy how much she seems to not enjoy Melville Dewey.
sentences.zh: 我没想到我还能更喜欢朱迪丝·弗兰德斯，但我真的很享受她看起来有多么不喜欢梅尔维尔·杜威。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so Melville Dewey, for those who don't know, is the inventor of the Dewey decimal system, or officially the Dewey Decimal Classification, or DDC,
sentences.zh: 那么梅尔维尔·杜威，对于那些不知道的人来说，是杜威十进制分类法的发明者，或者正式名称是杜威十进制分类法，简称DDC，

sentences.en: which is a sorting method for libraries that is still very common in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这是一种图书馆排序方法，在美国和当今许多图书馆中仍然非常普遍。

sentences.en: and many libraries today.
sentences.zh: 以及当今许多图书馆。

sentences.en: So apart from the objectionable way that Judith thinks he spells his name, what doesn't she like about him?
sentences.zh: 所以除了朱迪丝认为他拼写名字的方式令人反感之外，她还有什么不喜欢他的地方？

sentences.en: Well, she's got a few issues.
sentences.zh: 嗯，她对他有几个意见。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So basically, Melville Dewey was born in a small town in upstate New York in 1851.
sentences.zh: 基本上，梅尔维尔·杜威于1851年出生在纽约州北部的一个小镇。

sentences.en: And he actually changed the spelling of his name when he was quite young, because he was a fan of the movement at the time to simplify English spelling.
sentences.zh: 他在很年轻的时候就改变了自己名字的拼写，因为他是当时简化英语拼写运动的粉丝。

sentences.en: For a while, he even changed the spelling of his last name to D-U-I.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，他甚至把姓氏的拼写改成了 D-U-I。

sentences.en: That didn't stick?
sentences.zh: 那没坚持下去？

sentences.en: No, that one didn't stick.
sentences.zh: 不，那个没坚持下去。

sentences.en: Apparently, the bank refused to recognize his signature.
sentences.zh: 显然，银行拒绝承认他的签名。

sentences.en: Yeah, if you can't cash checks, then it doesn't stick.
sentences.zh: 是的，如果你不能兑现支票，那它就坚持不下去。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Dewey, D-E-W-E-Y, graduated from Amherst College in Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 所以杜威，D-E-W-E-Y，毕业于马萨诸塞州的阿默斯特学院。

sentences.en: And Judith Flanders says that soon after, he was made a librarian there.
sentences.zh: 朱迪丝·弗兰德斯说，不久之后，他就在那里当了图书馆员。

sentences.en: So he's still in his 20s, but he was asked to catalog its library.
sentences.zh: 所以他当时才20多岁，但被要求为图书馆编目。

sentences.en: The odds are pretty good.
sentences.zh: 机会很大。

sentences.en: He didn't know much about library classification.
sentences.zh: 他并不了解多少图书馆分类知识。

sentences.en: So he returned to the idea of a hierarchy of knowledge, which is based on the older classical liberal arts idea.
sentences.zh: 于是他回归了知识层级体系的理念，该理念基于更古老的古典博雅教育思想。

sentences.en: And it's important to point out that a lot of libraries back then, just like now, were already organized by subject, at least on some level.
sentences.zh: 值得指出的是，当时许多图书馆和现在一样，在某种程度上已经按主题进行了分类。

sentences.en: So all the calculus books would be in one place and all the American history books would be in another.
sentences.zh: 所以所有的微积分书籍会放在一处，而所有的美国历史书籍会放在另一处。

sentences.en: But Dewey took the basic idea and kind of went, let's say, mad with power.
sentences.zh: 但杜威采用了这个基本理念，并且可以说，他有点被权力冲昏了头脑。

sentences.en: He really believed, just like Coleridge, that all knowledge was connected in this elegant hierarchy.
sentences.zh: 他确实相信，就像柯勒律治一样，所有知识都以这种优雅的层级结构相互关联。

sentences.en: So in his new system, once you got to the subject area, it would just be divided into smaller subject areas,
sentences.zh: 因此在他的新系统中，一旦你进入某个主题领域，它就会被细分为更小的主题领域，

sentences.en: which themselves would be divided into yet smaller subject areas and so on and so on.
sentences.zh: 这些领域本身又会被进一步细分为更小的主题领域，以此类推。

sentences.en: So it becomes subjects all the way down.
sentences.zh: 所以它变成了层层嵌套的主题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this was his eponymous Dewey decimal system or Dewey decimal classification.
sentences.zh: 这就是以他名字命名的杜威十进制图书分类法。

sentences.en: And the reason it has the word decimal in there is because all of these subjects were assigned numbers.
sentences.zh: 之所以叫十进制，是因为所有这些主题都被分配了数字。

sentences.en: So, for example, the 500s are natural sciences, 590 is zoology, 595 is other invertebrates, 595.7 is insects, and eventually you get to butterflies if you follow along.
sentences.zh: 例如，500类是自然科学，590是动物学，595是其他无脊椎动物，595.7是昆虫，如果你顺着查下去，最终就能找到蝴蝶。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这很有道理。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: It doesn't seem like this is a real problem so far.
sentences.zh: 目前看来这似乎不是什么大问题。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，对，确实如此。

sentences.en: It wasn't totally a bad idea.
sentences.zh: 这并不完全是个坏主意。

sentences.en: And perhaps more importantly, at that time, it offered this kind of ready-made, off-the-rack solution for organizing books.
sentences.zh: 而且更重要的是，在当时，它为整理书籍提供了一种现成的、标准化的解决方案。

sentences.en: And it ended up getting picked up by a lot of these institutions throughout the second half of the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 它最终在19世纪下半叶被许多机构所采用。

sentences.en: So, you know, even if it's not perfect, it's used so widely that you could go to any library in the country and know where to find things.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，即使它并不完美，但由于使用极其广泛，你走进全国任何一家图书馆都能知道去哪里找书。

sentences.en: And that's probably its biggest advantage.
sentences.zh: 这大概是它最大的优势。

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: It's ubiquity, basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是它的普及性。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But Judith Flanders points out that it had a few big probleMs.
sentences.zh: 但朱迪丝·弗兰德斯指出，它存在几个大问题。

sentences.en: The benefit is, if you want to find out about the subject you work at, which its number is, you go to the shelves, and there are all the books.
sentences.zh: 好处是，如果你想了解你所研究的主题，找到对应的编号，去书架上就能看到所有的相关书籍。

sentences.en: So, it helps you find out about a subject more generally.
sentences.zh: 所以，它有助于你更全面地了解一个主题。

sentences.en: What it doesn't do is help you find a specific book.
sentences.zh: 但它无法帮你找到某本特定的书。

sentences.en: And this is sort of the crux.
sentences.zh: 这正是问题的关键所在。

sentences.en: So, if you're looking for a specific book, and you don't know where to classify it, you know, like in the 0.7, 0.6, 0.3 way, you know, it may be hierarchical, it may be logical.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你在找一本特定的书，却不知道该如何归类，比如在0.7、0.6、0.3这种分类方式下，你知道，它可能是层级的，也可能是逻辑的。

sentences.en: But it's not really all that intuitive of where you place every book in the human world.
sentences.zh: 但要把世界上每一本书都归入某个位置，这并不是那么直观。

sentences.en: No, it's not.
sentences.zh: 不，确实不是。

sentences.en: So, Dewey had no choice but to pair his system with a card catalog, which would tell you where to find the book.
sentences.zh: 所以，杜威别无选择，只能将他的系统与卡片目录结合使用，卡片目录会告诉你去哪里找书。

sentences.en: And do you want to guess what sorting method the Dewey Decimal System card catalog uses?
sentences.zh: 你想猜猜杜威十进制系统的卡片目录用的是什么排序方法吗？

sentences.en: I don't need to guess.
sentences.zh: 我不需要猜。

sentences.en: It's alphabetical order.
sentences.zh: 是字母顺序。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Our old friend.
sentences.zh: 我们的老朋友。

sentences.en: So, in the end, you know, as much as you want to order the world into these blocks of 100 numbers and subdivide it and subdivide it and subdivide it, when you get to the bottom,
sentences.zh: 所以最后，你知道，尽管你多么想把世界整理成这些100个数字的区块，并不断地细分、细分、再细分，但当你追溯到最底层时，

sentences.en: you have to get to alphabetical order.
sentences.zh: 你还是得回到字母顺序。

sentences.en: It sort of underlies everything.
sentences.zh: 它某种程度上是一切的基础。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Although it should be pointed out that Dewey managed to turn this to his advantage, because what Dewey did was to push the American Library Association,
sentences.zh: 尽管应该指出的是，杜威成功地将这一点转化为自己的优势，因为杜威所做的是推动美国图书馆协会，

sentences.en: which he had co-founded in 1876,
sentences.zh: 也就是他在1876年共同创立的那个协会，

sentences.en: to standardize the index card size and to then use a company he created called the Library Bureau to provide all the supplies needed to manage those card catalogs.
sentences.zh: 去标准化索引卡片的大小，然后利用他创立的一家名为“图书馆局”的公司，来供应管理这些卡片目录所需的所有用品。

sentences.en: Whoa.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That's very enterprising and a little bit sneaky.
sentences.zh: 这非常有商业头脑，但也有一点点狡猾。

sentences.en: I mean, is this the reason why Judith hates him?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这就是朱迪丝讨厌他的原因吗？

sentences.en: Like, because of this, you know, way of profiting from the library system?
sentences.zh: 是因为这种从图书馆系统中获利的方式吗？

sentences.en: No, it's not.
sentences.zh: 不，不是的。

sentences.en: Instead, it turns out that the card catalog is the least of the Dewey system's probleMs.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，卡片目录反而是杜威系统中最微不足道的问题。

sentences.en: Because when you start digging into its classification system, you soon realize that the problem was mostly Dewey himself and how he saw the world.
sentences.zh: 因为当你开始深入研究他的分类系统时，你很快就会意识到，问题主要出在杜威本人以及他看待世界的方式上。

sentences.en: All sorting systems have biases.
sentences.zh: 所有的分类系统都有偏见。

sentences.en: Dewey's has more biases than moSt.
sentences.zh: 而杜威的系统比大多数系统偏见更多。

sentences.en: And in the modern world, it is particularly troublesome.
sentences.zh: 在现代社会，这尤其令人困扰。

sentences.en: It is entirely Anglo-centric.
sentences.zh: 它完全是以盎格鲁-撒克逊为中心的。

sentences.en: It is almost comically Christian-centric.
sentences.zh: 它几乎滑稽地以基督教为中心。

sentences.en: So Christianity was given all the numbers between 200 and 289, whereas Islam is given only a single number, 297.
sentences.zh: 基督教占据了200到289之间的所有数字，而伊斯兰教只被分配了一个数字，297。

sentences.en: Oh, and women are originally categorized very neatly next to etiquette.
sentences.zh: 哦，女性最初被非常整齐地归类在礼仪旁边。

sentences.en: Bitter?
sentences.zh: 苦涩吗？

sentences.en: Me?
sentences.zh: 我吗？

sentences.en: No, not at all.
sentences.zh: 不，一点也不。

sentences.en: But beyond the system that he created, there was just Dewey the man.
sentences.zh: 但除了他创造的系统之外，还有杜威这个人本身。

sentences.en: Dewey himself was a mind-blowingly awful person.
sentences.zh: 杜威本人是一个令人震惊的糟糕透顶的人。

sentences.en: I say this with complete prejudice.
sentences.zh: 我带着完全的偏见说出这句话。

sentences.en: He founded the American Library Association, but was forced to step down when four women complained that he had assaulted them in a two-week period.
sentences.zh: 他创立了美国图书馆协会，但后来被迫辞职，因为有四名女性投诉他在两周内对她们进行了骚扰。

sentences.en: He was anti-Semitic, he was raciSt.
sentences.zh: 他有反犹太主义倾向，还是个种族主义者。

sentences.en: Even in anti-Semitic and racist days, he was considered to be pretty horrible.
sentences.zh: 即使在那个反犹和种族主义盛行的年代，他也被认为是非常恶劣的。

sentences.en: So he was also asked to stand down from his position as librarian for New York State for his Christian whites-only policies.
sentences.zh: 所以他后来也因为其“仅限白人基督徒”的政策而被要求辞去纽约州图书馆馆长的职务。

sentences.en: And if you can imagine in those times, it must have taken an awful lot for him to get to that stage.
sentences.zh: 如果你能想象在那个时代，他得做出多么过分的事情才会走到那一步。

sentences.en: Wow, I had some vague notion that Dewey was a problem, but I had no idea just how awful he really was.
sentences.zh: 哇，我之前模糊地知道杜威是个麻烦人物，但我完全没想到他竟然如此糟糕。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, he definitely was.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，他绝对是。

sentences.en: And because of all this undeniable awfulness, the American Library Association recently decided to take his name off their top leadership honor.
sentences.zh: 正因为这些不可否认的恶劣行径，美国图书馆协会最近决定将他的名字从其最高领导荣誉奖项中移除。

sentences.en: It used to be called the Melville-Dewey Medal, but in 2020, it was changed to the ALA Medal of Excellence.
sentences.zh: 它过去被称为“梅尔维尔·杜威奖章”，但在2020年，它被改为“ALA卓越奖章”。

sentences.en: But the thing is, even if Dewey himself isn't well-remembered, his system is still going strong.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，即使杜威本人不再被人们怀念，他的系统依然运行良好。

sentences.en: Despite the fact that it just doesn't work very well anymore.
sentences.zh: 尽管事实上它已经不太好用了。

sentences.en: But of course, undoing an entire library and recategorizing becomes very difficult, so people on the whole don't.
sentences.zh: 但当然，拆除整个图书馆并重新分类变得非常困难，所以人们总体上不会这么做。

sentences.en: So other sorting methods have been developed, and the Library of Congress has its own system.
sentences.zh: 因此，其他分类方法也应运而生，国会图书馆就有自己的系统。

sentences.en: But according to recent estimates, roughly 200,000 libraries in 135 countries still use the Dewey Decimal Classification.
sentences.zh: 但根据最近的估计，135个国家的约20万家图书馆仍在使用杜威十进制分类法。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So Judith hates him, but the world embraced him early, and then therefore we're just kind of stuck with Dewey's hierarchy, for better or worse.
sentences.zh: 所以朱迪丝讨厌他，但世界很早就接纳了他，因此无论好坏，我们都被杜威的层级体系困住了。

sentences.en: Very much so.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Thank you, Dan.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，丹。

sentences.en: Thanks, Roman.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，罗曼。

sentences.en: We are part of the Stitcher and SiriusXM podcast family.
sentences.zh: 我们是Stitcher和SiriusXM播客家族的一员。

sentences.en: Now headquartered six blocks north in the Pandora Building, in beautiful Uptown, Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 现在总部位于加利福尼亚州奥克兰市美丽的住宅区，在潘多拉大厦以北六个街区处。

sentences.en: You can find the show and join discussions about the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在Facebook上找到我们的节目并参与讨论。

sentences.en: You can tweet at me, at Roman Mars, on the show at 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 你可以在推特上关注我@RomanMars，或访问节目官网99pi.org。

sentences.en: We're on Instagram and Reddit, too.
sentences.zh: 我们也在Instagram和Reddit上。

sentences.en: You can find links to Stitcher shows I love, as well as every past episode of 99pi at 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 你可以在99pi.org找到我喜爱的Stitcher节目链接，以及99pi的所有往期节目。

sentences.en: Here's a fact I didn't know until I had kids in my 30s.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个我在30多岁有了孩子之后才知道的事实。

sentences.en: A, B, C, D, E, F, G.
sentences.zh: A, B, C, D, E, F, G。

sentences.en: Twinkle, twinkle, little star.
sentences.zh: 一闪一闪小星星。

sentences.en: Seriously, it blew my mind.
sentences.zh: 说真的，这让我大开眼界。

sentences.en: Stitcher, SiriusXM.
sentences.zh: Stitcher, SiriusXM。
